title.narrative: Public sector projects considering climate change criteria.

comment.narrative: In progress. The MEF's Investment Programming Department is implementing the new “Project Bank” registration tool: all public projects must be analyzed to determine whether they should be labeled as having activities that contribute to climate change mitigation and/or adaptation. Once labeled by the institution leading the project, they must be validated through an interactive process involving the MEF and the Ministry of the Environment. By the end of 2024, the MEF had implemented this approach for projects executed between 2019 and 2023. Out of a total of more than 2,000 public projects, 548 (around 25%) had been labeled and verified, involving 24 institutions (out of a total of 90). In the 2024 Bill, the estimated investment in CC is 16% ($1.071 billion) of the total budget ($6.542 billion). In principle, all new projects (100%) are now subject to this labeling (but are not yet validated). The MEF will communicate the updated data.

This trend is expected to continue and a greater proportion of efficient refrigerators will exist in the market in the medium term.
Since the approval of the national and regional technical regulations on energy efficiency for refrigerators, all equipment imported into the country has been considered efficient. title.narrative: Estimated efficient air conditioners in the country

comment.narrative: The acceleration in the incorporation of air conditioners in recent years, relative to the historical one, supports the increase in the proportion of efficient equipment of the total. In 2022 the proportion increased by 12.1%, in 2023 by 19.4% and in 2024 by 22.7%. The goal was reached by the end of 2024 through an estimate of the total renovation of efficient air conditioners, which comply with the standard. Since the approval of the national and regional technical regulations on energy efficiency for air conditioners, all equipment imported into the country has been considered efficient.

title.narrative: Electric buses of the Panama City public operator's fleet (MiBus) acquired or under procurement

comment.narrative:
IDB and MEF contract for the purchase of 55 bus units, endorsed by the CGR on April 21,2025.
Contract 001-2025 for the acquisition of 5 electric buses and 2 chargers, endorsed by the CGR on May 6,2025.
MiBus Note No. TMP-GPP-038-2025, in which MIBUS formally notifies the Prequalification Process for Public Tender No. 2025-2-81-01-08-LP004612: MiBus launched the prequalification process in September 2025 to acquire at least 53 electric buses and 17 chargers. The tender was published on PanamaCompra, and a homologation meeting was held on October 10. The current phase focuses on formal requirements; technical specifications will be addressed in the next stage.
MiBus has not yet been able to acquire the planned 55 electric bus units (financed by IDB loan) but is under the procurement process. In September 2025, Mibus started the prequalification process and expect to sign contract in March 2026. Additionally, a purchase contract of 5 units has been executed.

title.narrative: Number of charging stations per 100 km of the primary and secondary road network

comment.narrative: SNE has a georeferenced database with information on public charging stations for electric vehicles. It was considered that the primary and secondary road network is relatively constant. Active monitoring of the growth of the charging stations was carried out. SNE considered that a greater number of electric vehicles were expected in the fleet affected by the increase in charging stations.
